title: Root Vegetable Burekas with Roasted Mushroom Sauce
subtitle: thin wholemeal dough, cashew cream
description: Thin wholemeal pastry spirals filled with roasted kohlrabi, potato, spinach and fresh thyme, topped with cashew cream and served in a roasted oyster mushroom sauce. Start the dough the day before.

steps.text: Mix and knead the dough ingredients by hand until smooth and soft. Cover and rest for 30 minutes. Flatten, fold in half and in half again, return to the bowl, cover and refrigerate overnight. Take it out about 2 hours before working.
Divide the dough into 10 balls, rub each with olive oil, place in a lightly oiled tray, cover with cling film and rest for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a tray. Place the unpeeled kohlrabi and potatoes in the tray, sprinkle with 2 tablespoons salt and roast for 1 hour or until soft. Keep the oven on.
Peel the kohlrabi and potatoes, cut into medium cubes and combine with blanched, squeezed spinach, thyme, salt, pepper and 2 tablespoons olive oil.
Drain the cashews (soaked for 2 hours) and blend with lemon juice, 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 cup water until a smooth cream.
Stretch a dough ball into a very thin, almost transparent rectangle. Lay a 2 cm strip of filling along one long side, leaving 1 cm clear, and spread cashew cream on top.

Fold the edge over the filling and roll into a tight log, coil into a snail and place on a baking-paper-lined tray. Repeat with all the dough, spacing them 2 cm apart. Bake for 20 minutes until golden.
Meanwhile, fry the roughly chopped mushrooms in olive oil with salt and pepper in a wide pan over medium heat for about 12 minutes until soft and releasing liquid.
Arrange the pastries on a platter, pour the mushroom sauce over and serve hot.
